text.content:
Warm animal musk and woodsmoke roll up out of the dark ahead - the smell of a den that's been lived in a long time. The passage down is crude but well-worn, packed earth polished smooth by countless small feet, and fleece hangs drying from pegs driven into the walls like a butcher's rack turned inside out. A crooked sign is nailed over the threshold, its lettering hand-painted and confidently misspelled: "AL COM WELCUM - NO SPITING (aproved spitters only)." Somewhere below, something bleats. Something else laughs at it.

GM Notes

Read this once the party actually starts down: let the sign land as a joke before anything else - it sets the tone for the whole floor. Everything past here is played straight by its inhabitants and absurd to everyone else.

Milestone: The goblins of the Wool-Crowned Warrens answer to a self-crowned monarch who hands out rank based on one qualification: whether the herd llamas nuzzle you first. Deeper in (the Larders, past Room 6), that hierarchy is currently being reshuffled by a llama named Buttercup, whose favor is the single most valuable currency in the warren right now.

Secret: Half-buried under a collapsed shelf near the entrance is a waterlogged, wool-stuffed satchel: the journal of Old Tam, a shepherd-hermit who kept this stable-yard generations before the goblins moved in (Perception DC 13, or automatic if the party searches the entrance at all). His last entries describe a "hook that isn't a hook" he dug out of the yard wall, and a rhyme he used to keep it quiet. See the Boss Arena (Room 28) notes for what that's worth.

Subquest - The Sign: Purely cosmetic, but a good icebreaker: the sign is updated periodically by hoof-print veto - any rule a goblin scribe posts that Buttercup subsequently steps on gets struck out and rewritten. If the party lingers, have a goblin arrive to nervously repaint a line.
